Legal Practice Disclaimer & Bar Council Notice

Nepal Bar Council Code of Conduct 2051 Compliance Disclosure

Notice to All Visitors: The contents of this website are intended solely to provide general legal information and educational materials to the public in Nepal. Reviewing this website or communicating with our chambers electronically does NOT establish an advocate-client relationship.

1. General Legal Information Only

Substantive laws, procedural regulations, and limitation periods (Hadmyad) under the Muluki Civil Code 2074, Muluki Criminal Code 2074, and related Nepalese statutes are subject to legislative amendments and ongoing judicial interpretation by the Supreme Court of Nepal. While our research team endeavors to maintain accurate materials, you should never act or refrain from acting based solely on general website articles.

2. No Advocate-Client Privilege via Electronic Contact

Transmitting an email, calling our chambers telephone, or submitting an online consultation enquiry does not establish advocate-client privilege. An advocate-client relationship is created only after:

  • A thorough conflict-of-interest review has been completed by our registry;
  • Our advocates have formally agreed to accept representation; and
  • A legally binding engagement agreement and formal Vakalatnama (Power of Representation) have been executed in writing.

3. Absolute Prohibition of Outcome Guarantees

In accordance with Rule 32 of the Nepal Bar Council Code of Conduct 2051, advocates are strictly prohibited from guaranteeing judicial outcomes, case dismissals, bail grants, or financial awards. Every legal dispute depends on its specific documentary evidence, witness credibility, and judicial discretion.

4. Fee Estimates Subject to Statutory Court Rules

Any discussions of legal expenses or court fees on this site are descriptive only. Official court fees are governed strictly by the Court Fee Act 2017 (अदालती शुल्क ऐन, २०१७) and procedural rules of the relevant court.
